spans.s:
Haya denotes ‘horse’ in the Rigveda^1 and later.^2
1) v. 46, 1; vii. 74, 4; ix. 107, 25.
2) Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, vii. 47; xxii. 19, etc.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 231.

Hāyana denotes a ‘year,’ usually in compounds.^1 In the
Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā^2 and the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa^3 the term
appears as a designation of a species of red rice. As an adjec-
tive in the sense of ‘lasting a year’ or ‘recurring every year,’
it is applied to fever in the Atharvaveda.^4
1) Av. viii. 2, 21; śata-hāyana, ‘a
hundred years old,’ viii. 2, 8; 7, 22;
hāyanī, xii. 1, 36 (probably corrupt).
2) xv. 5.
3) v. 3, 3, 6 (the Taittirīya Saṃhitā,
i. 8, 10, 1, has instead mahā-vrīhi,
‘great rice’).
4) xix. 39, 10.
Cf. Schrader, Prehistoric Antiquities,
301.
